rules.statement: In cases of concealed fraud, the equitable principle can be applied even if there is no independent act of concealment when the tort itself is done furtively.
rules.supporting_quote: "Two men acting independently, steal a neighbour's coal. One is so clumsy in his operations, or so incautious, that he has to do something more in order to conceal his fraud. The other chooses his opportunity so warily, that he can safely calculate on not being found out for many a long day. Why is the one to go scot free at the end of a limited period rather than the other (loc. cit. p. 364)."
